title: Implement lightweight distributed request context envelope + SDK adapters for tracing
creator: Aria Patel
description: Problem: Our current request tracing and context propagation are inconsistent across runtimes (node/go/python) and HTTP/gRPC paths. Different services set nonstandard headers, we duplicate heavy x-headers, and SDK-instrumented clients unintentionally drop sampling flags when crossing internal proxies. Goal: introduce a compact 'request context envelope' (RCE) that travels with requests, provide lightweight middleware for service frameworks, and ship SDK adapters that automatically attach the RCE for outbound calls. The RCE must be backward-compatible with W3C traceparent/w3c baggage while minimizing header size and preserving sampling decisions, route metadata (region/tier), and a request TTL to prevent cross-tenant leakage.
acceptance_criteria: Define RCE wire format and mapping to existing w3c headers in a design doc and get PM + Security sign-off
Middleware exists for Node (express/fastify), Go (chi/http), and Python (fastapi/starlette) that reads + writes RCE and falls back to w3c traceparent if present
SDK adapters (js/pypi/go) automatically attach RCE on outbound HTTP/gRPC requests without user changes and expose opt-out flags
End-to-end integration test demonstrating trace continuity across three services + gateway without duplicating large baggage headers
Sampling flags persist through internal proxies and are visible in tracing UI; p95 latency for middleware <= 0.4ms added for common request path
Security review completed, threat model updated, and KMS usage documented for any signed/hashed fields
implementation_notes: RCE format chosen: base64-encoded compact payload containing trace_id(16), span_id(8), sampling(1), ttl(1), region(2), flags bitfield(1), and optional 8-byte application tag. Keep total <= 48 bytes before encoding
We will map RCE <-> w3c traceparent: trace_id/span_id/sampled map directly; baggage items remain optional and stored in our KV-caching layer rather than headers to limit header size
Use incremental rollouts: feature flag per service via console; default Off. Start with telemetry services and three core backend services in Canarian deploy
Middleware implementation should be nonblocking and avoid allocations on hot path; reuse object pools in Go and Node for header parsing
SDK adapters for JS should patch fetch and http.request; provide explicit export for customers who don't want automatic monkeypatching
Edge/gateway will be authoritative for region tagging when absent. Gateway will also enforce TTL decrements to avoid long-lived leaked contexts
We must add unit + integration tests for header truncation, deliberate malformed RCE, and TTL expiry behavior
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Created ticket after spike: confirmed inconsistent header patterns across 18 services (logs attached). Initial design sketch completed.
2026-02-18: Security kickoff meeting — agreed to keep RCE compact and avoid embedding PII. Security asked for signed digest for RCE in cross-DC hops; deferred to follow-up (ENG-7598).
2026-02-24: Prototype Node middleware implemented (express) and benchmarked — added ~0.35ms median overhead on local microbench (PR #10234).
2026-03-02: Cross-language API defined; Go parsing library started (pkg/requestctx). Added unit tests for base64 roundtrip and malformed header handling.
2026-03-07: PM review: requested explicit opt-out environment variable (REDWOOD_DISABLE_RCE) and updated rollout plan to include canary on dedicated customers first.

2026-03-10: Integration test: chained express -> gateway -> go-service preserved trace continuity in 20/20 runs. Noted that nginx proxy strips unknown headers by default; ops will add proxy config (OPS-441).
reviewer_feedback: PM (Lena Morales): Please ensure clear UX for customers to opt out and document any header size increases in migration notes.
Security (Evan Cho): Require automated fuzz tests for malformed RCE and add logging level that avoids printing raw header contents in prod.
Platform (Ravi Shah): Suggest using existing trace sampling service for sampling decision authority to avoid duplication; minor API tweak proposed in PR #10234.
Design (Maya Bloom): Prefer storing nonessential baggage in the new per-request KV cache instead of headers — reduces header footprint.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Enable RCE middleware on telemetry services + 3 backend services behind feature flag. Monitor tracing continuity and middleware latency for 72h.
Phase 2 (Ops alignment): Coordinate with gateway and nginx teams to preserve RCE header and set proxy passthrough. Disable RCE if proxies cannot be updated.
Phase 3 (SDK rollout): Publish JS/Go/Python adapters with opt-out env var and patch notes. Add migration guide to docs.
Phase 4 (Wide): Flip server-side default to On after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and full security checklist complete
